title: Cisco Duo Bulk Policy Deletion
exclusions: Single-policy deletions are not covered; they appear as `policy_delete` and belong in a general change report.
evidence: Alert rows listing the deleted policy names and the administrator, with the change ticket from the response.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a test Duo account create four throwaway policies and delete them together from the Policies page. After the next input interval the search returns one row with `policy_count=4` and the four names.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Delete two throwaway policies together. The `policy_bulk_delete` event is indexed but `policy_count` is 2, so no row is returned.

dataSources: `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input, Administrator log type (`GET /admin/v1/logs/administrator`).
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Duo input. Replaces the deprecated Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026).
spl:
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:administrator" action="policy_bulk_delete"
| rename username as user
| spath input=description
| rex field=policies max_match=0 "(?<policy_name>[^:,]+):\s+"
| eval policy_count=mvcount(policy_name)
| where policy_count > 3
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(policy_name) as policy_name by action actionlabel user admin_email policy_count
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
description: Finds Duo `policy_bulk_delete` actions that remove more than three policies at once. The search extracts each deleted policy name from the `policies` list in the change description and returns the administrator and the names.
value: Deleting several Duo policies at once can silently move applications back to the global policy, which is often weaker, or remove deny rules. It is a fast way for a rogue or compromised administrator to dismantle MFA controls, and rarely part of normal work.
implementation: Collect the Duo Administrator log with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input into `index=duo`. Tune the `policy_count > 3` threshold to your clean-up practice. Alert on each row.
visualization: Alert table: firstTime, user, admin_email, policy_count, policy_name. Supporting panel: policy deletions per administrator per month.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Planned policy consolidation** — tidy-up projects remove many obsolete policies at once. Match against the change ticket and the list of policies scheduled for removal.

2. **Test tenants** — lab Duo accounts are often reset in bulk. Exclude them by API hostname or index.

**Suppression:** an approved-change lookup keyed on administrator and date.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs. It replaces the Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026); disable the old connector's inputs after cutover so events are not indexed twice.
• A Duo Admin API application created by an Owner-role administrator in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. Record the integration key, secret key, and API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`), and grant it **Grant read log**.
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API hostname, and an accurate system clock on that host, because the Admin API signs every request with the current date.
• An index for Duo data (this page uses `index=duo`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the identity and SOC teams.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Duo card, and create an input with the integration key, secret key, and API hostname. Enable the Administrator log type and set the index to `duo`.
• The input reads `GET /admin/v1/logs/administrator` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator`, one event per administrator action, with `action`, `actionlabel`, `description` (a JSON string of the changed settings), `object` (the policy, user, or integration acted on), and `username` (the administrator).
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator action=policy_bulk_delete | spath input=description | table _time username policies` to see how your Duo release formats the `policies` list.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:administrator" action="policy_bulk_delete"
| rename username as user
| spath input=description
| rex field=policies max_match=0 "(?<policy_name>[^:,]+):\s+"
| eval policy_count=mvcount(policy_name)
| where policy_count > 3
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(policy_name) as policy_name by action actionlabel user admin_email policy_count
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
```

Understanding this SPL
• `action="policy_bulk_delete"` matches the single administrator event Duo writes for a multi-select delete.
• `spath` exposes `policies`, a string of `name: id` pairs; the `rex` with `max_match=0` captures every name into a multivalue field.
• `mvcount` counts them and `where policy_count > 3` keeps only larger deletions. Lower the threshold if your administrators rarely delete more than one policy.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Duo admin console (Admin Panel) under Reports > Administrator Actions: the bulk delete appears there with the same policy names.
• Check that `policy_name` on the alert has the same count as the policies listed in the raw `description`.
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days to confirm there are no collection gaps.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 15 minutes over the last 20 minutes and throttle on `policy_name` plus `username` for 24 hours, so one change produces one alert.
• Route to the identity team with the Duo change ticket number as a required field in the response, and send to Enterprise Security as a finding when ES is in use.
• Keep a 90-day table panel of all policy changes next to this alert, so reviewers can see what else the same administrator changed.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No Duo events and HTTP 401 in the input log under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/duo_splunkapp/`: wrong secret key, an API hostname from a different Duo account, or clock skew on the input host.
• HTTP 403: the Admin API application is missing **Grant read log**.
• HTTP 429: Duo rate-limits the log endpoints. Make sure the deprecated 3504 connector and the 7404 input are not both polling the same Admin API application.
• Duplicate rows after migration: the 3504 connector and the 7404 input are both enabled for the same log type.
• Rows show `policy_count` empty: the `policies` value does not use `name: id` pairs in your release. Adjust the `rex` to the format in one raw event.
grandmaExplanation: We alert when someone deletes a batch of Duo login rules at once, because that can quietly remove protections from many apps.
